result: Fixed two uninstrumented AB/BA processes completed successfully. Hyle public and aligned direct-nghttp2 both use the same single-worker two-fiber episode model. Point medians are close in these samples; no equivalence or pure scheduler-cost claim.

scope.payload: 4streams,256KiB request and response each, reverse pair completion

measured_boundary: Each call starts on the external caller: new socketpair/adopt, immutable workload references, session endpoints, ordinary spawn_task on the same persistent1worker Scheduler/IoContext, all request/response bytes with16KiB consume+both flow-control windows, reverse completion, final client-consumed Event, both joins, session/socket close, and remaining per-episode owner cleanup before return.
differences_kept_visible: Raw Episode zero-initializes two RawWire objects (128KiB per endpoint) inside every measured call, outside64KiB fiber stacks; raw allocation/container/codec/lifecycle work is still its own.
Raw direct-nghttp2 and Hyle public sessions differ in headers/body/session storage and host responsibilities. Matching execution model and aggregate counters does not isolate scheduler cost.
HyleHarness and an inactive persistent RawHarness thread are constructed for the lifetime of each process, identically for both measured arms. Construction/destruction is outside timed episodes.
functional_checks: Each process performs one untimed warmup per arm in its selected order using the exact timed workload and full original header/body/reversal oracle; raw warmup additionally checks both descriptorEBADF after joins. Timed calls retain full protocol validation/status/cleanup but omit extra fd observation. Both warmup stderr lines hyle4/raw4/raw_fds_closed=true and all timed calls succeeded.
instrumentation_removed: No raw_probe/owner/phase/dispatch/syscall counters, no resume interposition, no probe object, no dynamic-export or dl link flag; readelf verifies no own Fiber::resume definition or raw_probe symbols. Nanobench performance counters disabled; only normal epoch wall timing remains.
build: One fresh GCC14 Release/O3 C++23 TU and link using identical retained stage6 cached HTTP/nghttp2/nanobench/foundation closure. No SDK copy/download/configure/foundation rebuild. New TimerQueue implementation not rebuilt into this scheduler.
limitations: Only two process samples, nine epochs each arm; retain all epoch variation. No CI/equivalence claim, no repeat to chase a result.
